bugs: app/Jobs/SyncSupplierStock.php:13-16: #[Tries(3)] + #[Backoff] with no FailOnTimeout. A run that times out at 45 min is retried while the unique lock (#[UniqueFor(3600)]) is about to expire, so the next hourly dispatch can run alongside the retry. A worker killed mid-run gets the job back after retry_after=3600, at the same moment the next hourly dispatch lands. Either way two syncs can run at once, which the task forbids.

routes/console.php:22-25: carts:prune-abandoned runs dailyAt('01:00') with no ->timezone('Europe/Copenhagen'), so it runs at 01:00 in the app timezone (UTC), even though the business runs on Copenhagen time. The test name 'outside the DST window' is wrong because UTC has no DST.

v.rationale:
I reviewed impl-1, then impl-2, then impl-3. All three test suites pass (16, 25 and 11 tests). Each implementation got three or four throwaway probes, all deleted afterwards. Every prune handled 11k–20k rows correctly. Each report schedule fired at the right Copenhagen time in summer. An orphaned unique lock never blocked the next hourly dispatch.

impl-2 ranks first. It is the most carefully reasoned about the actual failure modes. It schedules everything in Copenhagen time at DST-safe hours. Its job uses Tries(1) and FailOnTimeout with Timeout < UniqueFor < 1h ≤ retry_after, so a run can't be doubled, and a crashed run frees the lock before the next hour. It also has the strongest Pest tests: DST datasets, a real multi-batch prune, and a check that the lock expires.

impl-3 ranks second. It gets the same essentials right and is simpler, but it uses older property-style conventions, Mail::raw without a Mailable, no scopes or factory states, and thinner tests.

impl-1 ranks third. Its Laravel 13 idioms are the most polished, but it has two real problems. Its retry policy (Tries 3 + Backoff, no FailOnTimeout, UniqueFor 3600) lets a retried or redelivered sync overlap the next hourly dispatch, which is exactly the doubling the task forbids. And its nightly prune ignores the Copenhagen timezone. It also adds --force/--dry-run/ConfirmableTrait ceremony, and its 'several batches' test never crosses a batch boundary.
